questions.stem: What does the latitude of a place measure?
options: Its angle east or west of the prime meridian
Its distance in kilometres from the equator
Its time difference from Greenwich, England
Its angle north or south of the equator
questions.explanation: Latitude is an angle from 0° at the equator to 90° at the poles, labelled N or S. The angle east or west of the prime meridian is longitude.

questions.stem: Through which place does the prime meridian, longitude 0°, pass?
questions.explanation: The prime meridian runs from pole to pole through Greenwich in London. Longitudes are measured up to 180° east or west of it. The International Date Line roughly follows 180°.

questions.stem: Sydney is at about 34°S, 151°E. What does this tell you about its position?
options: It is north of the equator and east of the prime meridian
It is south of the equator and west of the prime meridian
It is south of the equator and east of the prime meridian
It is south of the prime meridian and east of the equator
questions.explanation: The latitude, 34°S, places Sydney south of the equator, and the longitude, 151°E, places it east of the prime meridian. North and south refer to the equator, and east and west to the prime meridian.

questions.stem: Place A is at 20°N, 30°E and place B is at 15°S, 30°E. What is the difference in their latitudes?
questions.explanation: They are on opposite sides of the equator, so the latitudes add: 20 + 15 = 35°. 5° subtracts, which is only correct when both places are on the same side of the equator.

questions.stem: Which position is in both the Southern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere?
questions.explanation: S places it south of the equator, in the Southern Hemisphere, and W places it west of the prime meridian, in the Western Hemisphere. 23°S, 43°E is in the Eastern Hemisphere.

questions.stem: A map app shows a location's position coordinates as −33.87, 151.21. What position is this?
questions.explanation: Position coordinates list latitude first, then longitude. A negative latitude is south and a positive longitude is east, so this is 33.87°S, 151.21°E. A latitude can never exceed 90°, so 151.21 cannot be the latitude.

questions.stem: Using 15° of longitude = 1 hour, how many minutes of time does 1° of longitude represent?
questions.explanation: 1 hour = 60 minutes spread over 15°, so 1° represents 60 ÷ 15 = 4 minutes. 15 minutes reverses the relationship.

questions.stem: Two places on the equator have longitudes that differ by 60°. What is the time difference between them?
questions.explanation: Each 15° is 1 hour, so 60 ÷ 15 = 4 hours. 6 hours divides 60 by 10, and 15 hours confuses the degrees per hour with the answer.

questions.stem: Place A is at 150°E and place B is at 30°E. Using longitude only, when it is 10 am at A, what time is it at B?
questions.explanation: The longitudes differ by 120°, which is 8 hours. B is further west, so its time is behind: 10 am − 8 hours = 2 am. 6 pm adds the 8 hours, treating B as ahead.

questions.stem: Place A is at 135°E and place B is at 75°W. Using longitude only, when it is 9 pm Monday at A, what is the time at B?
questions.explanation: They are on opposite sides of the prime meridian, so the longitudes add: 135 + 75 = 210°, which is 14 hours. B is west, so it is behind: 9 pm Monday − 14 hours = 7 am Monday. 5 pm uses 135 − 75 = 60°.

questions.stem: Sydney is at about 151°E and Perth at about 116°E. What time difference does the longitude rule give, and how does it compare with the 2-hour difference in standard time?
options: 1 h 40 min, less than the time zones show
2 h 20 min, more than the time zones show
2 h 20 min, less than the time zones show
3 h 30 min, more than the time zones show
questions.explanation: 151 − 116 = 35°, and 35 × 4 = 140 minutes = 2 h 20 min. Time zones round to whole regions, so the official difference between AEST and AWST is 2 hours, a little less.

questions.stem: Two places' longitudes differ by 22.5°. What is the time difference between them?
questions.explanation: 22.5 ÷ 15 = 1.5 hours = 1 hour 30 minutes. 1 hour 50 minutes misreads 1.5 hours as 1 hour and 50 minutes.

questions.stem: What is 2.4 hours in hours and minutes?
questions.explanation: 0.4 of an hour is 0.4 × 60 = 24 minutes. 2 hours 40 minutes treats the decimal as minutes, but an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.

questions.stem: How many minutes are there in 3 hours 15 minutes?
questions.explanation: 3 hours is 3 × 60 = 180 minutes, plus 15 gives 195 minutes. 315 minutes treats each hour as 100 minutes.

questions.stem: A race takes 9000 seconds. How long is this in hours?
questions.explanation: There are 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds in an hour, and 9000 ÷ 3600 = 2.5 hours. 150 hours divides by 60 only once, which gives minutes.

questions.stem: What is 7:45 pm in 24-hour time?
questions.explanation: For pm times after 1 pm, add 12 to the hours: 7 + 12 = 19, giving 1945. 0745 is 7:45 am.

questions.stem: What is 0030 in 12-hour time?
questions.explanation: 0030 is 30 minutes after midnight, which is written 12:30 am. 12:30 pm is 30 minutes after midday, 1230 in 24-hour time.

questions.stem: What is 1205 in 12-hour time?
questions.explanation: 1205 is 5 minutes after midday. Times from midday until 1 pm are pm, so it is 12:05 pm. 12:05 am is just after midnight, 0005.

questions.stem: A flight departs at 2235 and arrives at 0610 the next day, both in the same time zone. How long is the flight?
questions.explanation: From 2235 to midnight is 1 h 25 min, and from midnight to 0610 is 6 h 10 min, a total of 7 h 35 min. 16 h 25 min subtracts 0610 from 2235 as if they were on the same day.

questions.stem: A movie starts at 7:50 pm and runs for 2 hours 25 minutes. When does it finish?
questions.explanation: 7:50 pm + 2 hours = 9:50 pm, and 9:50 pm + 25 minutes = 10:15 pm. 9:75 pm forgets that 60 minutes make an hour.

questions.stem: A worker starts at 9:40 am and finishes at 5:15 pm, with a 45-minute unpaid lunch break. How long is she paid for?
questions.explanation: 9:40 am to 5:15 pm is 7 h 35 min. Taking off the 45-minute break leaves 6 h 50 min. 7 h 35 min is the time at work, including the unpaid break.

questions.stem: How much time passes from 11:48 am to 3:12 pm?
questions.explanation: 11:48 am to 12:00 pm is 12 minutes, and 12:00 pm to 3:12 pm is 3 h 12 min, a total of 3 h 24 min. 3 h 36 min subtracts the minutes the wrong way round, 48 − 12.

questions.stem: Sydney and Melbourne are on UTC+10 (UTC+11 in daylight saving), Brisbane on UTC+10, Adelaide on UTC+9:30 (UTC+10:30 in daylight saving), Darwin on UTC+9:30 and Perth on UTC+8. Outside daylight saving, it is 3 pm in Sydney. What time is it in Perth?
questions.explanation: Sydney is UTC+10 and Perth is UTC+8, so Perth is 2 hours behind: 3 pm − 2 hours = 1 pm. 5 pm treats Perth as ahead, but places further west are behind.

questions.stem: Sydney and Melbourne are on UTC+10 (UTC+11 in daylight saving), Brisbane on UTC+10, Adelaide on UTC+9:30 (UTC+10:30 in daylight saving), Darwin on UTC+9:30 and Perth on UTC+8. Outside daylight saving, it is 4 pm in Brisbane. What time is it in Adelaide?
questions.explanation: Adelaide is UTC+9:30, half an hour behind Brisbane's UTC+10, so it is 3:30 pm. 4:30 pm puts Adelaide ahead instead of behind.

questions.stem: Which two of these states and territories do not observe daylight saving?
questions.explanation: Queensland, Western Australia and the Northern Territory stay on standard time all year. New South Wales, the ACT, Victoria, Tasmania and South Australia move their clocks forward one hour.

questions.stem: Sydney and Melbourne are on UTC+10 (UTC+11 in daylight saving), Brisbane on UTC+10, Adelaide on UTC+9:30 (UTC+10:30 in daylight saving), Darwin on UTC+9:30 and Perth on UTC+8. During daylight saving, it is 9 am in Sydney. What time is it in Brisbane?
questions.explanation: In daylight saving Sydney moves to UTC+11, but Brisbane stays on UTC+10, so Brisbane is 1 hour behind: 8 am. 9 am would be correct only outside daylight saving.

questions.stem: Sydney and Melbourne are on UTC+10 (UTC+11 in daylight saving), Brisbane on UTC+10, Adelaide on UTC+9:30 (UTC+10:30 in daylight saving), Darwin on UTC+9:30 and Perth on UTC+8. During daylight saving, it is 6 pm in Melbourne. What time is it in Perth?
questions.explanation: Melbourne is UTC+11 in daylight saving and Perth stays on UTC+8, a difference of 3 hours, so it is 3 pm in Perth. 4 pm uses the standard-time difference of 2 hours.

questions.stem: Sydney and Melbourne are on UTC+10 (UTC+11 in daylight saving), Brisbane on UTC+10, Adelaide on UTC+9:30 (UTC+10:30 in daylight saving), Darwin on UTC+9:30 and Perth on UTC+8. During daylight saving, it is 2 pm in Darwin. What time is it in Adelaide?
questions.explanation: Both are UTC+9:30 in standard time, but in daylight saving Adelaide moves to UTC+10:30 while Darwin does not, so Adelaide is 1 hour ahead: 3 pm. 2 pm ignores that only South Australia changes its clocks.

questions.stem: Sydney and Melbourne are on UTC+10 (UTC+11 in daylight saving), Brisbane on UTC+10, Adelaide on UTC+9:30 (UTC+10:30 in daylight saving), Darwin on UTC+9:30 and Perth on UTC+8. During daylight saving, a flight leaves Perth at 11:20 pm local time and lands in Sydney at 6:35 am the next day, local time. How long is the flight?
questions.explanation: In daylight saving Sydney (UTC+11) is 3 hours ahead of Perth (UTC+8). The clock times differ by 7 h 15 min, so the flight takes 7 h 15 min − 3 h = 4 h 15 min. 5 h 15 min uses the standard-time difference of 2 hours.

questions.stem: What does it mean for a place to be on UTC+8?
options: It is 8° of longitude east of the prime meridian
It is 8 hours ahead of Australian Eastern Standard Time
Its time is 8 hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time
Its time is 8 hours behind Coordinated Universal Time
questions.explanation: UTC is the world's reference time, and UTC+8 means local time is 8 hours ahead of it. A place 8 hours ahead of UTC lies roughly 8 × 15 = 120° east, not 8°.

questions.stem: Guatemala is on UTC−6 and Malaysia is on UTC+8. When it is 9 am in Guatemala, what time is it in Malaysia?
questions.explanation: The difference is 8 − (−6) = 14 hours, and Malaysia is ahead, so 9 am + 14 hours = 11 pm. 11 am uses a difference of 2 hours, from 8 − 6.

questions.stem: A city is on UTC−5. Sydney is on UTC+10. When it is 7 pm Tuesday in Sydney, what is the time in the city?
questions.explanation: The difference is 10 − (−5) = 15 hours, and the city is behind, so 7 pm Tuesday − 15 hours = 4 am Tuesday. 2 pm Tuesday uses only 5 hours.

questions.stem: Sydney is on UTC+11 during daylight saving. A person in a city on UTC+1 wants a call to reach Sydney at 8 am Wednesday, Sydney time. When should the person call, in local time?
questions.explanation: Sydney is 11 − 1 = 10 hours ahead, so subtract 10 hours from 8 am Wednesday: 10 pm Tuesday. 6 pm Wednesday adds the 10 hours, treating the city as ahead.

questions.stem: A flight leaves Sydney (UTC+10) at 10:00 am Monday and takes 14 hours to reach a city on UTC−7. What is the local time when it lands?
questions.explanation: Departure is 10:00 am − 10 h = 00:00 Monday UTC. Landing is 14 hours later, 14:00 Monday UTC, which is 14:00 − 7 h = 7:00 am Monday local time. The clock shows an earlier time than when the flight left.

questions.stem: Ignoring political boundaries, what UTC offset matches a place at 120°W, using 15° = 1 hour?
questions.explanation: 120 ÷ 15 = 8 hours, and places west of the prime meridian are behind UTC, so UTC−8. UTC+8 would be a place at 120°E.

questions.stem: It is 0930 UTC. What is the time in Brisbane, on UTC+10, in 24-hour time?
questions.explanation: Brisbane is 10 hours ahead of UTC: 0930 + 10 hours = 1930. 2330 subtracts the hours the wrong way round from 0930 and lands the day before.
